title: Doba Milsztejn’s Polish passport
note: Born 1895, birthplace and residence Opalin; three accompanying children: Rywka, Szul-Beniamin and Pinchas. The photo and title pages are supplied scans.
locator: Description, photograph and children pages; passport series I, no. 354856

title: Passport identity and residence page
note: Doba Milsztejn, resident in Opalin; three children. See the accompanying photograph page.

title: South African settlement visa
note: British Passport Office, Warsaw, 21 August 1934. This is a visa, not evidence of the date of arrival in South Africa. The adjoining stamps concern the European journey.
locator: Passport pages 18–19

title: German transit visa
note: Warsaw, 3 September 1934. Permission for passage through Germany; it is not a German permit to emigrate from Poland.
locator: Passport page 21

title: Polish border-control stamp
note: Departure stamp at Zbąszyń, 6 September 1934. The low-resolution scan limits finer reading.
locator: Passport page 5

title: Passport observations and emigration approval
note: Passport valid for one journey abroad; Warsaw emigration-inspector stamp, 1 September 1934.
locator: Passport page 7

title: Cancelled visa page
note: An uncompleted South Africa visa form marked cancelled. Do not mistake it for the completed settlement visa.
locator: Passport page 15

title: Gloucester Castle passenger manifest, 1934
note: London departure, 13 September 1934; Union-Castle line. Doba and the three children contracted to land at Cape Town. The ship’s overall destination is entered as Beira. Ages: 38, 14, 11 and 7.
locator: The National Archives, BT27/1400; P.M.25, alien passengers; digitised by Findmypast; family-supplied scan

title: Rywka Milsztejn identification card
note: An identification card, not a passport. Birth: 19 November 1919. The ship and date entry reads Gloucester Castle, 7 October 1934. This places her below fifteen on arrival.
locator: Ethan Cohen’s family history, p.14; embedded scan extracted unchanged

title: Opalin school photograph
note: Mark tentatively identifies Riva in the front row, second from the right, holding flowers. The identification and date are not independently verified.

title: Nutke: portrait and handwritten reverse
note: Family identification: Nutke Milstein, Moshe’s brother and Riva’s uncle. His formal given name and individual death record remain unknown. The handwriting has not received a verified full translation.

title: Moishe Milstein: family portrait
note: Identified by Mark Cohen as Moishe (Moshe) Milstein, Doba’s husband. Supplied as a one-page PDF titled “Zaida Moishe Milstein.pdf”. Photograph date and place are not established.

title: Reverse of Moshe’s photograph
note: Identified by Mark as Moshe Milstein, Doba’s husband. Opalin and a date apparently in 1935 are visible; the dedication and precise day/month need expert reading.

title: Riva Gilinsky — Ethan Cohen’s family history
note: Undated, 15 pages. Authored by Ethan, Mark’s son. First-person relationships refer to Ethan. Includes an Ancestry tree, family photographs and early research; superseded details are discussed on this site.
locator: Especially pp.1, 6–14; treat as a secondary family compilation

title: Morris Millstein death certificate, 1935
note: Registration 6091: died 5 September 1935, Johannesburg Hospital; registered 6 September. Age 41, married, Poland-born vegetable hawker; 31 Bezuidenhout Street, Troyeville. Ulcer surgery and haemorrhage fit the testimony, but the record does not name Doba or parents.
locator: Image 3109 of 3222; index 742P-426Z. Local copy is a browser screenshot, not a full-resolution original.

title: Mina Milstein and Elias Spitalnik, 1937
note: Johannesburg certificate 1322, 11 August 1937: Mina, 24, Poland-born; Elias, 35, Lithuania-born tailor. Mina’s address matches Morris’s 1935 address. Strong candidate for Minnie; parents not named.
locator: Image 1159 of 2946, image group 008161332; index 6ZC9-N33R. Saved browser screenshot.

title: Aron Milstein gravestone
note: Death 19 February 1977; Hebrew patronymic identifies father Moshe. Burial register: 20 February, H 2215. Strong match to Arke through the tapes.
locator: Johannesburg Chevrah Kadisha, H 2215

title: Minnie Spitalnik gravestone
note: Died 2 August 1997; Menucha daughter of Leib. Burial 4 August 1997, U 818 Ext D.

title: Isaac Slot gravestone
note: Died 26 July 1952; burial register gives 31 July, B 347. The stone does not individually name his children or establish Bulawayo as his death place.

title: Johannesburg Chevrah Kadisha burial search
note: Live surname searches recorded 18–19 November 2026: Doba, Aron, Minnie, Isaac, Hela and Harry. Hela: Chaya Rivka bas Binyomin, 26 November 2004, E1025 Ext D; Harry: 22 January 1985, adjacent E1025 Ext C. Re-run surname searches; no persistent individual result URLs.

title: Morris Millstein memorial index
note: Westpark Jewish section, 1894–6 September 1935. No photograph, individual grave number or named relatives was found. Its date differs from the civil death date; it is not a gravestone reading.

title: Mendel Lederer’s Warsaw bakery, 1928
note: Księga adresowa Polski: Lederer Mendel, Ogrodowa 24, under Piekarnie / Boulangers. The year is 1928; 1918 is the printed page number.
locator: Printed p.1918, PDF p.60. A short extract is also bundled.

title: Mendel Lederer: baker testimony
note: Born 1880 in Opalin, baker, wife Riva; Warsaw before and during the war, death place entered Warsaw ghetto. Submitter Doba Kam, sister-in-law. She has not been identified as Doba Slot.
locator: Yad Vashem 335860; original form inspected, browser screenshot saved

title: Mendel Lederer: second testimony
note: Born 1885 in Opalin, merchant, wife Rivka Fuks; Warsaw, then Treblinka, 1942. Submitter Menukha Il, relative. Parent and child fields blank. Possible duplicate of the baker, not merged.
locator: Yad Vashem 1118855; original form inspected, screenshot saved

title: Jospa / Yosefa Lederer testimony
note: Włodawa-born, age 45; parents Eliezer and Chaya, husband Beniamin; Opalin residence and death place. Sister Brakha Berland submitted it. The original lists three children; marital handwriting may read widow, whereas the index says married. No death year is supplied. A source-provided scan was also downloaded from the viewer for this edition.
locator: Yad Vashem 2024866; widow reading remains provisional

title: Freida Lederer testimony
note: Opalin, parents Beniamin and Yosefa, husband Eliahu. Submitter Berka Berland, aunt. Strong candidate for Hela’s sister Frida, without an explicit Hela link.

title: Chuma / Khuma, born Lederer
note: Opalin, parents Beniamin and Yosefa, husband Tzvi, married surname unknown. Submitter Brakha Berland, aunt. Possible Nechama from the tape; not established.

title: Pesl Sosne / Sosna, born Lederer
note: Opalin-born; husband Asher; Maciejow residence and death. Submitted by daughter Ana Roiter. A collateral lead, not yet proved to be Doba’s sister.

title: Chaya Dwora Alter, born Milshtein
note: Born 1882, Opalin; parents Israel and Zissel, husband Naftali. Dorohusk before the war, Maciejow during it; testimony gives death 1941 in Ukraine. Submitted by granddaughter Hadasa Nechushtan.
locator: Combined person 13465449; underlying testimony 1867215

title: Yisrael Alter’s Dorohusk memoir
note: Names mother Chaya Dvora and siblings; immigration to Palestine in 1936, aged twenty. The Warsaw police episode connects it strongly to the filmmaker’s father’s account. Return-visit chronology and number of surviving brothers remain discrepant across accounts.
locator: Dubienka / Skryhiczyn / Dorohusk memorial book, Dorohusk section, p.169

title: Naftali Alter interviewed by Asaf Nevo
note: Israel Hayom, 16 January 2020. Identifies father Israel, plasterer then building contractor, and mother Pnina; recounts the father’s Warsaw incident. The son repeats his father’s account, rather than providing a second eyewitness.

title: Naftali Alter — Israel Film Archive
note: Identifies the filmmaker, born Tel Aviv in 1947. The biography itself does not establish the older Milstein genealogy.

title: Vyshnivka, formerly Opalin — killing-site profile
note: Yahad–In Unum gives 2 October 1942, 582 victims, Jewish cemetery, a German unit from Lyuboml assisted by Ukrainian police. Its quoted witness and the linked clip are not safely treated as the same testimony.
locator: Profile 328; quoted testimonies 1441/1442; clip reference 1443U

title: Opalin witness video 1443U
note: Six-minute public clip, recorded 25 April 2012. English-subtitle review: title says born 1934; witness says ten; estimate 860 victims differs from profile 582. One-shooter claim is attributed to a friend. No family member is named.

title: Doba Slot estate notice, 2783/77
note: Original Gazette now downloaded and visually checked: Doba Slot, formerly Milstein, born Ledere; estate 2783/77; 36 Umgeni Road, Emmarentia; Berger & Berger. The notice is not the full estate packet.
locator: Government Gazette 5715, 19 August 1977, printed p.104 / PDF p.104. Full Gazette also bundled.

title: Doba’s estate: film-range lead
note: Film 2276122 / image group 7748578 covers estates 1961/77–360/78. The catalogue explicitly restricts digital access. Numerical inclusion does not prove that the individual packet survives.
locator: FamilySearch catalogue 1162069; no original packet inspected

title: Isaac Slot estate: TAB MHG 5056/52
note: Official National Archives description, ZA TAB MHG_0_5056/52_1. No digital object attached; full file not obtained.

title: Annie Slot, born Camberg: death notice
note: Died 4 August 1941, Johannesburg, 53, Edinburgh-born; husband Isaac, estate agent; children Hayme (reading provisional), Paul and Leslie, born 16 May 1923. Plausible earlier Slot household, not yet joined conclusively to Doba.
locator: Image 1380 of 2092. Saved screenshot; does not assign sex to the children.
